digest.component_or_area: Jira DC harness field-readiness gate and epic-link probe
propositions: The harness session-start gate waits for Epic Link and Epic Name fields at setup, but GreenHopper only provisions those fields when the first Software project is created, creating an ordering deadlock where the gate blocks the action that enables the capability.

Runs 30975323866 (600s budget) and 30978613228 (1800s budget) both expired with byte-identical empty-customfield inventories and an idle container 29 minutes after startup, proving the blockage is action-dependent not time-dependent.

Run 30981084637 demonstrated that 180 seconds of quiet waiting produced zero field provisioning, but project creation provisioned all 13 custom fields within 0.0512 seconds, conclusively refuting the budget hypothesis.
The epic-link probe has the same ordering bug: it calls _await_named_fields before project creation, causing probe runs 30944211742 and 30930839323 to fail identically.

The decision rule in not_ready_message incorrectly attributes zero customfield_* entries to plugin startup delay rather than the absence of a Software project, causing misdiagnosis and pointing readers at a non-existent budget problem.
